newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: After surging four cents against the dollar on Monday, to its best level in 3-1/2 months, the rand retraced some of its heady gains towards the close as players took profits and importers were lured into the market.
Bonds, although still firm and hovering around four month highs, followed the rand off its best levels also succumbing to late profit-taking.
But dealers said the currency would resume its move towards even stronger levels on Tuesday.
"Guys did not test the 4.5250 level properly today. Usually there are three proper tests. I think we will see this tomorrow, but if it does not break then we will weaken again," a trader said.

The rand ended at 4.5335/5365 on the dollar after briefly touching a 4.5235 bid in the afternoon, its strongest level since touching 4.5225 on October 15 last year. The unit finished at 4.5635/5665 on Friday.
"We had to have a retracement. If you have a 400 point move in one day, you are going to see some profit taking," a dealer said.
He said that importers, who were earlier absent from the market, were also sniffing around at the attractive lower levels.
Large-scale local sales of dollars by exporters, with mining houses fingered as active in the market, as well as offshore greenback sales were earlier said to be behind the rand's steady climb.
An announcement that U.S. soft drinks giant Coca-Cola intended to invest 1.25 billion rand in South Africa over the next five years provided a further fillip shortly after noon.
"With the ways things are going, it may test that magical 4.50 level in the next seven days," another dealer said.
Economists have attributed the strong recovery in the rand to an improvement in foreign perceptions of South Africa.

"Basically they believe that the fiscal deficit will come in on target, privatisation will be announced and while growth is low, they think that interest rates should fall and so set in place the scene for stronger growth in 1998," ING Barings economist Hania Farhan said.
Against the crosses the rand firmed a touch against the British pound to last trade at 7.3039/3137 from 7.3064/3158 on Friday and at 0.3630/3633 from 0.3586/3590 against the mark.
